laws.title: City flower
laws.content:
The flower known by the botanical name of "Nerium," commonly known as Oleander, is hereby declared to be the official flower of the city and as such may be displayed in the streets and parks of the city, and otherwise appropriately used.

(Code 1956, § 1-7)
laws.plain: Oleander is New Orleans' official city flower, and the city may use it to decorate streets and parks.

laws.title: §44.0101 Common Drinking Cup Prohibited
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful to provide for common use, or to use in common any cup, glass or other receptacle used for drinking purposes in any hotel, restaurant, saloon, soda fountain, theatre, public hall, private or public school, church, hospital, club, office building, park, playground, lavatory, barber shop, or any other place, building, room or conveyance frequented by the public.

(*“Common Drinking Cup Prohibited” added 2–10–1953 by O–5486 N.S.*)
laws.plain: Businesses and public places can't set out a shared cup or glass for people to drink from in common.

laws.title: Method of Preservation
laws.content:
- Maintain the appearance of the house and grounds as closely as possible to its present condition.
- Maintain the landscaped character of the grounds and their physical and visual relationship to the shoreline environment.
- Perpetuate the sense of place by using the site for Hawaiian cultural events.
laws.plain: Keep the historic house and grounds looking close to how they are now, preserve the landscaping and its link to the shoreline, and keep using the site for Hawaiian cultural events.

laws.title: By-right public, civic, and institutional uses
laws.content:
By-right public, civic, and institutional uses within the M3 General Industrial District are as follows:

(1) Armory.

(2) Electric transformer station.

(3) Fire or police station, post office, courthouse, and similar public building.

(4) Gas regulator station.

(5) Governmental service agency.

(6) Power or heating plant with fuel storage on site.

(7) Telephone exchange building.

(8) Water works, reservoir, pumping station, or filtration plant.

(Code 1984, § 61-10-55; Ord. No. 11-05, § 1(61-10-55), eff. 5-28-2005)
laws.plain: In the M3 heavy-industrial zone, these public facilities are allowed without special approval: armories, electric and gas stations, fire and police stations, post offices, courthouses, power and heating plants, phone exchanges, and water works.

laws.title: Maintenance
laws.content:
All buildings, structures, or ground areas used as a heliport or helistop shall be maintained in a safe and sanitary condition. All equipment or machinery required by the Construction Code or the Fire Code for a building, structure, or ground level area when erected, altered, or repaired shall be maintained in good working order. The licensee shall be responsible for the maintenance of all buildings, structures, or ground areas used as landing areas by helicopters.

(Ord. No. 2015-1103, § 2(Exh. A), 11-10-2015)
laws.plain: Heliports and helipads must be kept safe and clean, all required equipment kept in working order, and the license holder is responsible for that upkeep.

laws.title: Safety
laws.content:
The following safety measures shall be provided:

1. A skilled swimmer shall be present at all times when the pool is in use.

2. The pool area shall be equipped with one or more throwing ring buoys not more than 15 inches (381 mm) in diameter and having 60 feet (18.2 m) of 3/16-inch (4.7 mm) manila line attached, and one or more light but strong poles with blunted ends and not less than 12 feet (3658 mm) in length, for making reach assists or rescues.

3. No diving board or platform more than three feet (914 mm) above water level shall be installed.

4. Life-saving equipment shall be provided and maintained so as to be immediately available for use in an emergency.

(Added Coun. J. 10-14-21, p. 37722, Art. XII, §1)
laws.plain: When the pool is open a skilled swimmer must be on hand. The pool needs rescue gear (a ring buoy on a rope and a long reach pole), diving boards can't be more than three feet above the water, and lifesaving equipment must be ready to grab in an emergency.

laws.title: General requirements concerning arrangement and location of structures; landscaping
laws.content: In addition to minimum yard and building spacing requirements specified in this part, all buildings and other structures and landscaping shall be located and arranged on lots as to provide safe and convenient access for fire protection, servicing and off-street parking located on the premises. (For additional requirements see Tree Preservation Ordinance, City of Atlanta.) (Code 1977, § 16-28.005)
laws.plain: Buildings, other structures, and landscaping must be placed on a lot so fire trucks, service vehicles, and on-site parking can get in and out safely.

laws.title: C. Parking
laws.content:
Except where superseded by this subsection, the regulations of 33.266 apply to all parking.

1. **Minimum required parking spaces.** No minimum parking is required.

2. **Maximum allowed parking.** The maximum number of parking spaces allowed is stated in Table 597-3.

3. **Surface parking limitation.** No more than 25 percent of the total number of parking spaces on a site can be in surface parking. Industrial uses and sites 20,000 square feet or less in total site area are exempt from this requirement.

597-17
laws.plain: For these sites no minimum parking is required, the maximum is set by a table, and no more than 25% of spaces can be surface parking (industrial uses and small lots are exempt).

laws.title: Tax part of operating overhead
laws.content:
It is not the intention of this Chapter 5.38 that the taxes herein levied upon persons engaging in business be construed as taxes upon the customers of such businesses, but that taxes shall be levied upon, and collectible from, the person engaging in the business activities herein designated and that such taxes or fees shall constitute a part of the operating overhead or cost of doing business of such persons.

(Ord. 126108, § 1, 2020.)
laws.plain: The business tax is charged to the business, not to its customers; it's meant to be treated as part of the cost of doing business.

laws.title: § 217-28. Declaration of emergency
laws.content:
**A.** The Mayor of the Village may declare a state of emergency in cases of flood, serious fire or other extreme public emergency whenever conditions resulting therefrom create a dangerous driving condition within the Village. During the existence of such emergency, no vehicle shall be parked or abandoned upon that portion of the public highway or highways affected by the conditions resulting from flood, serious fire or other extreme public emergency.

**B.** The chief of police may declare a state of snow emergency whenever in his judgment snow has created dangerous driving conditions within the Village. During the existence of a snow emergency, no vehicle shall be parked or abandoned upon any Village streets.
Village of Lake Placid, NY

§ 217-29

PARKING

§ 217-33
laws.plain: The Mayor can declare an emergency during a flood, serious fire, or similar crisis, and the police chief can declare a snow emergency. While one is in effect, you can't park or leave a vehicle on the affected streets.

laws.title: § 14-318. Landfill: Industrial
laws.content:
(a) An industrial landfill must:

(1) be a part of the City’s Solid Waste Plan;

(2) comply with all applicable federal, state, and local environmental, health, and other laws, rules, and regulations; and
(3) obtain a state reuse disposal permit and all other applicable state and local permits.

(b) An industrial landfill may not accept:

(1) residential solid waste;

(2) municipal solid waste; or

(3) rubble or land-clearing debris.

(c) Materials must be deposited in layers, covered with suitable cover material to a depth and at a frequency sufficient to control disease, vectors, and odors and in a manner that protects the environment.

(d) An industrial landfill must be located, conformed, drained, and managed so that it will not constitute a source of water pollution.

(e) An industrial landfill must be screened from public view in accordance with the requirements of the Baltimore City Landscape Manual.

(Ord. 16-581; Ord. 17-015)
laws.plain: An industrial landfill must be part of the city's waste plan, follow all environmental laws, and hold the required permits. It can't take household or city trash or construction debris, must cover its waste often enough to control odors and pests, be run so it doesn't pollute water, and be screened from public view.

laws.title: § 9-702. Responsibility for Abatement. [Ord. 1387, 9/8/1992, Section 702]
laws.content: It shall be the duty of any person creating a nuisance, responsible for permitting a nuisance or any owner or occupant of land upon which a nuisance exists to remove such nuisance. The abatement of a nuisance(s) shall be in accordance with the notice and prosecution provisions of this ordinance or in accordance with the provisions of any other applicable ordinance(s) providing for the abatement of specific nuisances.
laws.plain: Whoever creates or allows a nuisance, and the owner or occupant of the land it's on, must remove it, following the notice and enforcement steps in this or another applicable ordinance.

laws.title: § 7.40.020. Establishment of the voucher program
laws.plain: Government agencies and nonprofits can hand out cab vouchers worth a one-way fare in town. Each voucher must show details like who issued it, the cab company, the date, the fare, the passengers, and the pickup and drop-off. The provider pays the cab company back directly.

laws.title: Notice to Abate
laws.content: Upon discovery of any junk motor vehicle or junk machinery stored upon private property within the corporate limits of this city in violation of section 5-5-8 of this chapter, the mayor or a peace officer shall within ten (10) days notify in writing the owner of said motor vehicle (who is the owner or person in control of the property upon which it is stored) that: a) the motor vehicle constitutes a nuisance under the provisions of this chapter; b) that the owner must remove or repair the motor vehicle or machinery in accordance with the terms of section 5-5-10 of this chapter; and c) that failure to remove or repair the motor vehicle or machinery will be sufficient cause for its removal by the city at the owner’s cost. (1975 Code)
laws.plain: If a junk vehicle or junk machinery is found stored on private property against the rules, the mayor or a police officer has 10 days to notify the owner in writing that it's a nuisance, that they must repair or remove it, and that the city can otherwise haul it away at the owner's expense.

laws.title: Grant of Authority
laws.content: The town hereby grants to the franchisee the right and privilege to engage in the business of operating and providing a CATV system within the town, and for that purpose to erect, install, construct, repair, resite, replace, reconstruct, rebuild, maintain and retain in, on, over, under, upon, across and along any streets, alleys, avenues, parkways, lanes, bridges, utility easements, laid out or dedicated and all extensions thereof and additions thereto in the franchise area, such poles, wires, cable, conductors, ducts, conduits, vaults, manholes, pedestals, amplifiers, appliances, attachments, and other property as may be necessary and appurtenant to the CATV system and in addition, so to use, operate, and provide similar facilities or properties rented or leased from other persons, including, but not limited to, any public utility or other grantee franchised or permitted to do business within the town. (1976 Code § 5.45.020)
laws.plain: The town grants the cable company the right to run a cable-TV system, including putting up and maintaining poles, wires, and related gear along streets, alleys, and easements, and using facilities leased from other utilities.

laws.title: A8.590-6 Retiree Benefit Adjustments
laws.content:
No agreement reached by the parties and no decision of the arbitration board shall reduce the vested retirement benefits of retirees or employees of the fire department, police department or of the sheriff department. Retirement and death allowances shall continue to be set and adjusted pursuant to Chapter Five of this Article, except that the amount to which said allowances are set and adjusted for uniformed employees of the police department and fire department shall not be less than the amount said allowances would be if the salaries of the uniformed forces in the police and fire departments continued to be set pursuant to Charter Section 8.405. Any agreement or decision of the arbitration board altering vested retirement benefits shall be subject to the written approval of the individual beneficiaries thereof.

(Amended March 2004)
laws.plain: No labor agreement or arbitration decision can cut the retirement benefits that police, fire, and sheriff retirees and employees have already earned. Those benefits keep being set under existing rules, and any change to vested benefits needs each affected person's written approval.

laws.title: Water Rights
laws.content:
A. Any subdivider of land not located within the original place of Cloudcroft as shown on the original plat map filed of record, prior to the approval of a final plat, shall be required to transfer to the village of Cloudcroft sufficient water rights to serve all lots in the subdivision being presented for approval.

B. "Sufficient water rights" shall be defined as the right to divert from either surface or underground sources at least 0.45 acre-feet per annum per lot.

C. Such water rights to be acceptable to the village must have been accepted for filing as prima facie evidence of such right with the state engineer of the state of New Mexico.

D. Such water rights shall be deemed to be acceptable when the state engineer of the state of New Mexico has recognized or authorized a transfer of such water rights the place of diversion, change of purpose of use to municipal so that such water rights may be incorporated and used in the Cloudcroft municipal water system by diversion from a surface source or a completed functional well for diversion from an underground basin.

E. In lieu of a transfer of water rights, the subdivider may pay to the village four thousand five hundred dollars
laws.plain: Before a new subdivision outside old Cloudcroft is approved, the developer must transfer enough water rights to serve every lot (at least 0.45 acre-feet per lot per year), properly filed with the state engineer, or instead pay the village $4,500.

laws.title: § 8-41. Traffic and parking controls. [Code 1982, § 7.02]
laws.content:
(1) The director of public works, in coordination with the chief of police, shall maintain the Administrative Code of Traffic and Parking Regulations for the City of Marshfield, to include the establishment of traffic control signage and the establishment and enforcement of speed limits, parking and through-street designations, heavy traffic routes, one-way street and alley designations, and all other necessary and convenient regulations for the control of traffic in and about the City of Marshfield, and including parking limitations.

(2) All additions, deletions or amendments to the Administrative Code of Traffic and Parking Regulations shall be submitted to the board of public works for review and approval, subject to the further review and approval of the council. Upon approval of the board of public works, and concurrence of the council, such additions, deletions or amendments to the Administrative Code of Traffic and Parking Regulations shall become enforceable, and violations of such code shall be deemed a violation of the Municipal Code, subject to penalties as provided in this chapter of the Municipal Code.
laws.plain: The public works director and police chief keep the city's traffic-and-parking rulebook, setting signs, speed limits, parking, one-way streets, truck routes, and the like. Changes go to the public works board and council for approval, and breaking the rules is a code violation with penalties.

laws.title: Fire Code
laws.content:
SECTION:

4-4-1: Adoption Of Fire Code

4-4-1: ADOPTION OF FIRE CODE:

There is hereby adopted, for the purpose of prescribing regulations governing conditions hazardous to life and property from fire or explosion, the most current version of the International Fire Code, as adopted by the State of Idaho, including all appendices thereto, and the same is hereby adopted and incorporated as though fully set forth at length herein.

The City Clerk shall maintain not less than one duly certified copy of the most current version of the International Fire Code at the Office of the City Clerk for use and examination by the public during normal business hours, in accordance with Idaho Code, section 50-901. (Ord. 917, 1-2-2018)
laws.plain: Grangeville adopts the current International Fire Code (as adopted by Idaho) to govern fire and explosion hazards, and the City Clerk keeps a copy available for the public to read during business hours.

laws.title: Addition of Section 123 of 2015 Michigan Mechanical Code, Special Inspectors Registration
laws.content:
In accordance with Section 8b(11) of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1508b(11), the City adds Section 123, Special Inspectors Registration, to the 2015 Michigan Mechanical Code, which provisions were contained in the 1984 Detroit City Code prior to July 31, 2001, and concern administration and enforcement:

123 SPECIAL INSPECTORS REGISTRATION

123.1 Certificate of Registration required. It shall be unlawful for any person to engage in the business of or to act in the capacity of a special inspector for an insurance company under Rules 75, 79, and 81 of the Michigan Boiler Rules, being R408.4075, R408.4079, and R408.4081 in the Michigan Administrative Code, as promulgated by the Director of the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs under Section 4 of the Michigan Boiler

CD8:174
laws.plain: Detroit adds a registration rule to the state mechanical code: you can't work as a special inspector for an insurance company under the state boiler rules unless you hold a certificate of registration.

laws.title: Fees
laws.content:
The fees charged by the department of public works for a tour planner license shall be as follows:

(1) **Category 1 Tour Planner Licenses**:

a. Initial license issuance and annual renewal: $500.00.

(2) **Category 2 Tour Planner Licenses (Tour Company)**:

a. Initial license issuance and annual renewal: $1,000.00.

(Code 1956, § 12-236; M.C.S., Ord. No. 21480, § 1, 4-1-04; M.C.S., Ord. No. 27526, § 2, 9-14-17; M.C.S., Ord. No. 28624, § 1, 3-11-21)
laws.plain: A tour-planner license costs $500 a year; a tour-company license costs $1,000 a year, for both the first license and each renewal.

laws.title: Dedication of Revenue
laws.content:
(Amended by Ordinances 191736 and 191957, effective January 1, 2025.)

**A.** Portland Permitting & Development may retain up to four percent of the taxes collected for payment towards the Bureau’s administrative expenses related to collection and distribution of the tax.

**B.** For the tax imposed on residential improvements, the net revenues will be distributed as follows:

1. 15 percent of net revenue will be remitted to the Oregon Department of Housing and Community Services to fund home ownership programs.

2. 50 percent of net revenue will be transferred to the Portland Housing Bureau Inclusionary Housing Fund to fund finance-based incentives for programs that require affordable housing.

3. 35 percent of net revenue will be transferred to the Housing Bureau Inclusionary Housing Fund to support the production and preservation of affordable housing units at and below 60 percent median family income.

**C.** For the tax imposed on commercial improvements, 100 percent of net revenue will be distributed to the Housing Bureau Inclusionary Housing Fund to support the production and preservation of affordable housing units at and below 60 percent median family income.
laws.plain: The permitting bureau may keep up to 4% of this tax for its costs. The rest of the residential-improvement tax is split among state home-ownership programs and two affordable-housing funds, and all of the commercial-improvement tax goes to affordable housing at or below 60% of median income.

laws.title: Amendment of registration statements
laws.content:
In the event any substantial change or addition occurs with respect to the information required by this article to be contained in the registration statement, an amendment to the statement shall be filed with the board of ethics within 14 days.

(Prior code § 26.2-24; Added Coun. J. 5-16-90, p. 16204; Amend Coun. J. 5-17-00, p. 32667, § 1)
laws.plain: If something important in your filed registration statement changes, you have 14 days to file an amended statement with the board of ethics.

laws.title: Transitional provisions; legal nonconformities under prior ordinance
laws.content:
Any legal nonconformity under Ordinance No. 390-G, as amended, being the Official Zoning Ordinance of the City of Detroit, which was repealed on the effective date of the ordinance from which this chapter is derived, will also be a legal nonconformity under this chapter, as long as the situation that resulted in the nonconforming status under the previous zoning ordinance continues to exist. Where a nonconformity under the previous zoning ordinance becomes conforming because of the adoption of the ordinance from which this chapter is derived, the situation will no longer be a nonconformity.

(Code 1984, § 61-1-12; Ord. No. 11-05, § 1(61-1-12), eff. 5-28-2005)
laws.plain: If a property was a legal nonconforming use under the old zoning ordinance, it stays legally nonconforming under the new one as long as that situation continues. If the new ordinance makes it conforming, it's no longer a nonconformity.

laws.title: Center Amenities
laws.plain: Country-town and rural commercial centers should be landscaped and welcoming, with features like street trees, mini-parks, wider sidewalks for cafes, pedestrian lighting, and street furniture such as benches and bike racks.

laws.title: License fees
laws.content:
The license year for all fees required under this Chapter 6.270 shall be from January 1 to December 31. All license fees shall be payable on an annual basis, which fees shall be as follows:

A. Adult entertainment premises license: $905 per year;

B. Adult entertainer’s license: $170 per year;

C. Adult entertainment manager’s license: $216 per year; and

D. The Director shall review annually the licensing fees in this Section 6.270.060 and may make any necessary adjustments in a Director’s Rule to ensure the fees achieve full cost recovery of the Department’s administrative, enforcement, and other regulatory costs based on, but not limited to consideration of the following factors:

1. The projected costs and annual budget allotted for administrative, enforcement, and regulatory costs across the adult entertainment industry; and

2. The need for increased enforcement to reduce illegal activity.

(Ord. 125703, § 3, 2018; Ord. 125449, § 8, 2017; Ord. 120978 § 3, 2002: Ord. 118395 § 14, 1996: Ord. 116466 § 1, 1992: Ord. 114225 § 1(part), 1988.)
laws.plain: Yearly license fees: $905 for an adult-entertainment venue, $170 for a performer, $216 for a manager. The director reviews the fees each year and can adjust them to cover the city's regulation and enforcement costs.

laws.title: § 5-5. Applications
laws.content:
(a) The application for a variance must be submitted to the Planning Department and, to the greatest extent possible, must comply with the provisions of this Division I.

(b)

(1) The Planning Department must notify the applicant, in writing:

(i) of the increased premium rates for flood insurance; and

(ii) that construction below the level of the base flood increases risks to life and property.

(2) This notification must be maintained as part of the record required in § 5-7 {"Record of variance actions"} of this subtitle.

(City Code, 1976/83, art. 7, §7(e), (f); 2000, art. 7, §5-5; Ord. 88-188; Ord. 11-516; Ord. 14-208)
laws.plain: A flood-zone variance application goes to the Planning Department and should follow this division's rules. The department must tell the applicant in writing that flood-insurance premiums will rise and that building below the flood level increases risk, and must keep that notice on file.

laws.title: Damage to airport property
laws.content:
Damage, destruction or defacement of airport property is covered by O.C.G.A. § 16-7-24. No person shall alter, make additions to or erect any building or sign on the airport or make any excavations on the airport or willfully abandon any personal property on the airport. Any person causing or being responsible for the injury, destruction, damage or disturbance shall report such damage to the office of the aviation general manager and, upon demand by such office, shall reimburse the city for the full amount of damage.

(Code 1977, § 12-3004)
laws.plain: Don't damage, deface, or build on airport property, dig there, or abandon belongings there. Anyone who causes damage must report it to the airport's general manager and, if asked, repay the city in full.

laws.title: § 16-277. Removal and Relocation of Facilities
laws.content: A Permittee may, or as may be determined by the Borough Manager or his/her designee, be required, at its expense, to promptly protect, support, temporarily disconnect, relocate in, or remove from, Rights-of-Way, lands or places, any Facilities of Permittee whenever required by the Municipality upon reasonable notice applicable to the conditions warranting such disconnection and as then determined by Borough Manager or his/her designee by reason of traffic conditions, public safety, Rights-of-Way construction or any other reasonable public purpose.
laws.plain: A permit holder must, at its own cost, move, support, disconnect, or remove its equipment from public rights-of-way whenever the borough reasonably requires it for traffic, safety, construction, or other public reasons.

laws.title: Notice of removal
laws.content:
(a) Whenever an officer removes a vehicle from a street as authorized in this article, and the officer knows or is able to ascertain the name and address of the owner thereof, such officer shall immediately give or cause to be given notice in writing to such owner of the fact of such removal, and the reasons therefor, and of the place to which such vehicle has been removed. In the event any such vehicle is stored in an authorized garage, a copy of such notice shall be given to the proprietor of such garage.

(b) Whenever an officer removes a vehicle from a street under this article, and does not know and is not able to ascertain the name of the owner, or for any other reason is unable to give the notice to the owner as hereinbefore provided, and in the event the vehicle is not returned to the owner within a period of three days, then and in that event the officer shall immediately send or cause to be sent written report of such removal by mail to the state department of highways and public transportation in Austin, Texas, and shall file a copy of such notice with the proprietor of any authorized garage in which the vehicle may be stored. Such notice shall include a complete descrip
laws.plain: When an officer tows a vehicle and can find the owner, they must promptly notify the owner in writing of the tow, the reason, and where it's stored. If the owner can't be found and the vehicle isn't returned within three days, the officer must report it to the state and notify the storage garage.

laws.title: §33.0106 Name of Business
laws.content:
It is unlawful for any *permittee* to operate any police-regulated business or engage in any police-regulated occupation under any name or designation other than the name or designation on the *police permit*. This section does not preclude the use of stage names by persons issued *police permits* under Divisions 28 and 36. (*“Transition Provisions” repealed; “Name of Business” added 11-20-2000 by O-18885 N.S.*) (Amended 11-8-2021 by O-21385 N.S.; effective 12-8-2021.)
Ch. Art. Div.
3 3 1 3
San Diego Municipal Code
laws.plain: A permit holder can't run a police-regulated business under any name other than the one on the permit, though performers may still use stage names.

laws.title: § 18-71. Bulk and density standards. [Ord. No. 1240, 11-13-2012]
laws.content:
(1) All developments shall comply with the standards listed for each zoning district in Article II, except as noted in this chapter.

(2) The conversion of any accessory building into a dwelling so as to accommodate an increased number of dwelling units or families shall be permitted only within a district in which a new building for similar occupancy would be permitted under this chapter.

(3) Additions or conversions of any accessory building into a dwelling shall comply with the requirements governing new construction in such district, including minimum lot size, lot area per dwelling unit, building of lot coverage, dimensions of yards and other open spaces, and off-street parking.
laws.plain: All developments must meet the zoning district's standards. Turning an accessory building into housing is only allowed where a similar new building would be, and such conversions must meet the same rules as new construction (lot size, yards, parking, and so on).

laws.title: Notice to Abate
laws.content: Upon discovery of any junk motor vehicle or junk machinery stored upon private property within the corporate limits of this city in violation of section 5-5-8 of this chapter, the mayor or a peace officer shall within ten (10) days notify in writing the owner of said motor vehicle (who is the owner or person in control of the property upon which it is stored) that: a) the motor vehicle constitutes a nuisance under the provisions of this chapter; b) that the owner must remove or repair the motor vehicle or machinery in accordance with the terms of section 5-5-10 of this chapter; and c) that failure to remove or repair the motor vehicle or machinery will be sufficient cause for its removal by the city at the owner’s cost. (1975 Code)
laws.plain: If a junk vehicle or junk machinery is found stored on private property against the rules, the mayor or a police officer has 10 days to notify the owner in writing that it's a nuisance, that they must repair or remove it, and that the city can otherwise haul it away at the owner's expense.

laws.title: § 265-29. Surviving, un-remarried spousal exemption for volunteers killed in the line of duty
laws.content:
**A.** The property tax exemption authorized by this article and granted to an enrolled member of an incorporated volunteer fire company, fire department, or incorporated voluntary ambulance service shall, upon application, be continued to such deceased enrolled member’s un-remarried spouse if such member is killed in the line of duty, provided that:

(1) Such un-remarried spouse is certified by the authority having jurisdiction for the incorporated volunteer fire company, fire department, or incorporated voluntary ambulance service as an un-remarried spouse of such enrolled member who was killed in the line of duty;

(2) Such deceased volunteer had been an enrolled member for at least five years; and

(3) Such deceased volunteer had been receiving the exemption prior to his or her death.

**B.** Any exemption pursuant to this § 265-29 shall terminate upon remarriage of the previously un-remarried spouse.
laws.plain: A property-tax exemption for a volunteer firefighter or ambulance member continues for their un-remarried spouse if the member is killed in the line of duty, provided the spouse is certified, the member had served at least five years, and was already receiving the exemption. It ends if the spouse remarries.

laws.title: Operation of Motorized Nonstandard Vehicles
laws.content:
A. Definition: A motorized nonstandard vehicle is a vehicle upon which a person may be transported that:

1. Is propelled by its own power;
2. Has a wheelbase of less than forty inches (40") and a wheel diameter of less than ten inches (10"); and
3. Does not display a certification in accordance with federal safety guidelines, or have a seventeen (17) digit VIN assigned by a manufacturer in accordance with federal guidelines.

B. Operation Authorized: The operation of a motorized nonstandard vehicle on the ways of this state open to the public located within the town of Terry is specifically authorized. (Ord., 6-8-2010)
laws.plain: A 'motorized nonstandard vehicle' is a small self-powered vehicle (short wheelbase, tiny wheels) with no federal safety certification or manufacturer VIN. Operating one on public roads in Terry is specifically allowed.

laws.title: § 4.20.130. Registration – Suspension or revocation
laws.content:
Whenever any person fails to comply with any provision of this chapter or any rule or regulation of the mayor relating thereto, the mayor, upon hearing, after giving such person ten days’ notice in writing, specifying the time and place of hearing and requiring him to show cause why his certificate of registration should not be revoked or suspended, may revoke or suspend any one or more of the certificates of registration held by such person. The notice may be personally served or served by registered or certified mail directed to the last known address of the person. A dealer whose certificate of registration has been previously suspended or revoked or who fails initially to register as a dealer shall pay the city a fee of one hundred dollars for the renewal, issuance or reissuance of a certificate of registration.

(prior code § 3.32.160; Ord. 78-17 § 3(part); Ord. 88-7 § 3(part))
laws.plain: If a registered dealer breaks the rules, the mayor can suspend or revoke their registration after 10 days' written notice and a hearing. A dealer whose registration was suspended or revoked, or who never registered, pays a $100 fee to renew or reissue it.

laws.title: Mobile Home Subdivisions
laws.content:
A. General: Mobile home subdivisions shall be subject to any requirements set forth in the zoning ordinance.

B. Special Requirements: The following special requirements shall apply to mobile home subdivisions:

1. A minimum acreage of five (5) acres will be required for planned unit mobile home subdivisions.

2. Screening from adjacent areas other than subdivisions of the same type by aesthetically acceptable fences, living plant material and/or existing natural vegetation or landscaped berms to be maintained by the home owner’s association.

3. Creation of a home owner’s association to assure all common areas are adequately maintained. (Ord. 561, 4-18-1983)
laws.plain: Mobile-home subdivisions must follow the zoning ordinance, plus: planned ones need at least five acres, must be screened from neighboring areas with fences or landscaping, and must form a homeowners' association to maintain the common areas.

laws.title: Penalty for Failure to PAY
laws.content: A penalty of ten percent (10%) of the amount owed to the Village under this Chapter shall be assessed upon any person who shall fail to pay the license fee in accordance with the terms of this Chapter and prior to the date on which the tax or fee is due as specified herein. Thereafter, the Village Clerk/Treasurer shall assess an additional penalty of one percent (1%) per month, for each portion thereof after the first month that the license fee is unpaid. The Village Clerk/Treasurer shall not issue any occupation license or license of any kind until the license fee, plus all assessments and penalties due herein, are paid. (1976 Code § 9-3-9; amd. 2000 Code)
laws.plain: Pay your license fee late and you owe a 10% penalty, plus another 1% for each month it stays unpaid. The village won't issue any license until the fee and all penalties are paid.

laws.title: A8.523-2 Eligibility
laws.content:
The Department of Human Resources shall certify to the Retirement System that a member is eligible to purchase service credit pursuant to eligibility criteria set forth in Charter Section A8.365-2. Provided, however, that the Department of Human Resources shall only certify a member as eligible to purchase service credit with the Retirement System if he or she took Unpaid Parental Leave prior to July 1, 2003, and if he or she returned to work for the City for at least six months immediately after the expiration of his or her Unpaid Parental Leave. The Retirement System shall rely on the certification from the Department of Human Resources to determine eligibility to purchase service credit for Unpaid Parental Leave.

(Added by Proposition G, 11/4/2008)
laws.plain: HR certifies to the Retirement System whether a member may buy service credit for unpaid parental leave. It only certifies members who took that leave before July 1, 2003 and returned to work for the city for at least six months afterward.

laws.title: § 2-21. Minors under 16
laws.content:
It is unlawful for the proprietor or person in charge of any premises on which there is a pinball machine (as that term is described and characterized in this article), which is or should be licensed under this article, to permit any person under 16 years of age to operate that device at any time.

(City Code, 1966, art. 15, §73(1st sen.); 1976/83, art. 15, §93(1st sen.); Ord. 56-664; Ord. 99-526)
laws.plain: A place with a licensed pinball machine can't let anyone under 16 play it, at any time.
